transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Honestly, I'm just feeling completely empty and sad all the time lately, and I don't know what to do. For the past month, I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love doing. It just feels like there is nothing left inside me.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life, or did they come on without a clear trigger?
I don't think there was any specific trigger or major change that started this. It feels like these feelings just came on out of nowhere without any real cause.
Before this past month, had you been feeling down or low most days for two years or longer, even if it was milder than now?
No, definitely not. Before this past month, I hadn't felt down or low like this at all. These feelings of sadness and emptiness are completely new to me and only started recently.
Over this past month, have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness?

I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or appetite, to be honest. As for my concentration or feeling guilty, I'm not really sure about those either. It's mostly just been that heavy feeling of emptiness and sadness.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to die, hurting yourself, or that life isn’t worth living?

Yes, over the past month I've been having thoughts of wanting to die, and I often wish I just wouldn't wake up in the morning. I don't have any specific plan to hurt myself, but everything feels so empty and it just feels like life isn't worth living anymore.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or impulsive than usual?

Yes, actually, before this low point I had a period of about five months where I felt incredibly energized and happy for no reason. I felt like I had endless energy and was constantly starting new activities because I just couldn't sit still.
During that five-month high-energy period, did you ever have hallucinations, hear voices, or develop beliefs that others said were unrealistic or not true?

Yes, during those months I actually started hearing voices that other people couldn't hear. I also truly believed I had special powers and a unique mission to accomplish, even though my family kept telling me it wasn't real.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing voices or had unusual beliefs even when you were not feeling especially high, energized, or depressed?

Yes, I actually did have a period like that for about two or three weeks. My mood had completely leveled out and I felt totally normal, but I was still hearing those voices and having those strange beliefs. It was really confusing because I wasn't feeling high or low at all during that time.
Over the whole course of your illness, have mood episodes like depression or high-energy periods been present for most of the time that you’ve also had the voices or unusual beliefs?

Yes, those high-energy periods have definitely been present for the majority of the time I've been dealing with these issues overall. I did have that one month of feeling really down, and a brief time where I had the voices and beliefs without any mood symptoms at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a clear manic syndrome lasting about five months with elevated mood/energy and psychotic symptoms, followed by a major depressive episode lasting one month with suicidal ideation. Crucially, there was also a 2–3 week period of hallucinations and delusional beliefs in the absence of mood symptoms, which supports schizoaffective disorder rather than a primary mood disorder with psychotic features. Mood episodes have been present for the majority of the illness duration, consistent with the bipolar type of schizoaffective disorder.
